chunk_findings.detail: The regression test never inspects the reply of the overtaking `update --globs` command. It only asserts that the DX update returns status 0 and then runs a separate `brief` command. The stated bug is that the update reply is silent: “the update succeeded with no note … the reply should name the waiter it overtakes.” No part of the diff changes the update-reply code path, and the test never looks at the `out` value from that `update` call, so the test can pass while the overtaking update still silently omits `bhy`. This does not exercise/refute the reported defect.

chunk_findings.detail: `_overtaken_waiters` is called after a retarget but never compares the pre-update and post-update waiter/glob sets. It returns every standing waiter currently visible to `WG.waiting_for` for the item, so an `update --globs` that keeps an already-held glob and adds a new one will also report waiters that were already waiting on that item before the command. Concrete input: item A already holds glob `a`, and agent B already has a standing wait on `a`; running `ddflow update --globs a b` is a widening that keeps `a` and adds `b`. `_overtaken_waiters` returns B because A still holds `a`, and `update_message.py:27` prints `overtook: B (B) (a standing wait now waits on you for a glob this just granted)` even though `a` was not just granted and B was not overtaken by this update. The helper needs the delta between the old and new waiter set/globs, not all current waiters.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:_overtaken_waiters

chunk_findings.detail: `_overtaken_waiters` reports every current `WG.waiting_for` hit after retarget, with no diff against the globs already held, and `update_message.py` then prints that as "overtook" / "a glob this just granted". After the bug's overtake, BHY is already a standing waiter on DX for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/` while DX holds `brief.py`. A later `update DX --globs ddflow/tools/foo.py,ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py,ddflow/tools/other.py` still returns those same waiters, so the reply names bhy/BHY as overtaken by this grant even though the overlap existed before the call. The new tests only cover the first widen, so they stay green on that false note.

chunk_findings.detail: `new_globs = [g for g in accepted if g not in old_globs]` uses exact string membership, but the project’s globs overlap hierarchically (this same change imports `globs_overlap` because `ddflow/api/lifecycle/` overlaps `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`). Concrete input: an item already holds `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`; the update widens it to `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`, and a waiter has a standing ask for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`. The accepted directory is not an exact member of `old_globs`, so `new_globs` contains it; `globs_overlap` then matches that waiter, and the reply names it as overtaken even though the item already held the asked-for file and granted no new part of the waiter’s ask. The previous fix is incomplete: the computation must account for overlapping held coverage, not merely differing strings.

chunk_findings.detail: The overtake set is every waiter in the folded log whose ask overlaps a newly accepted glob and does not overlap an old held glob. `item_id` is never used, and nothing requires `w.holder` to be this item after `L.retarget`. Given this item's old globs `[]`, accepted `["ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py"]`, and a standing waiter `B-hy-stop-protocol` whose holder is still some other item because that other item holds `ddflow/api/lifecycle/other.py` while the ask is `ddflow/api/`, `globs_overlap` is true for the new file, the waiter is not in `blocked_before`, and the update reply claims that wait "now waits on you". It does not.

chunk_findings.detail: `_overtaken_waiters` records `item` as the waiter and `holder` as who the wait points at. After a successful retarget that holder is the item that just widened, not the waiter. Input: updater `DX-wait-cycle-followups`, waiter `B-hy-stop-protocol`, post-retarget `holder=DX-wait-cycle-followups`. The reply leads with `overtook:  DX-wait-cycle-followups (B-hy-stop-protocol)`, so the party named as overtaken is the grantee. The same swap is in `_waiting_on_you`: `{w['holder']} has waited ... for the files {iid} holds (for {w['item']})` states that the holder waited for files the holder already holds, and only parenthesizes the waiter.

chunk_findings.detail: The test that is supposed to pin hierarchical subsumption never uses a hierarchical ask. DX already holds `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py` and BHY's refused update asks for that same string; DX then sets globs to `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`. An implementation that only skips a waiter whose ask is an exact member of the old glob list still prints no "overtook" here, so the assertion passes. The input that stays green while the exact-membership bug remains: BHY's standing ask is `ddflow/api/lifecycle/` (already blocked by the held file via overlap) and DX widens from `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py` to `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`. That accepted directory is not an old glob, and the ask is not equal to `brief.py`, so the reply can still name BHY as newly overtaken and this file never checks it.
